system.summary: A one-to-one letter table, a reciprocal half-alphabet on the 22-letter Italian alphabet (a-m against n-z, plain z written k), with numbers for doubled letters, nulls 24, 25, 27, about 30 code numbers for words, and L with a superscript for persons and places.
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the rows of key.tsv; sign names are the transcriber's. The ligature S also gives ss, so ss has two forms. Unknown codes: 43, 46, 95, 96, L^22, L^30, L^54, L^6. Context only: 44 sua maesta, L^o imperatore, 55, 63, 69. Catalogue 1554 adds 13, 26, 29, 36, L^3, L^7, L^8, all open, which is why the counts here include them. In 1554, 43 may be sua santita, a proposal.

prior_solution.where: Checked 2-3 Nov 2026 by web searches (Ercole to Ferrante, Murphy, Furlotti, Solmi, Capasso): no edition or decipherment of these letters found. Luzio (1922) describes the copialettere as scattered. Not opened: Murphy, Ruling Peacefully; the Furlotti and Solmi works; Ercole's copialettere at Mantua, which may hold clear minutes. Whether these letters are printed is unknown. Catalogue 1554: three web searches on 2-3 Nov 2026 found no edition or decipherment; no book was opened.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (key frozen before tests, blind passes, independent check). AI agents transcribed, built the key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention.

solution.what: Fetched the Estense leaves by IIIF. The two target letters have no decipherment on the leaves. cc. 103r/104r and cc. 109r-v/107r-v are cipher and decipherment pairs of July 1544.
c. 103r transcribed twice; 34 of 1,166 signs differ; settled on 2x enlargements.
Global alignment of c. 103r with c. 104r gave the table, then frozen. A rebuild with no table as input agrees on 19 of 20 signs.

Held-out c. 109r R01-R07 read blind to the clear text, against c. 107: 83.0% in runs of 3+ (200 shuffled tables max 26.1%), 240 of 279 aligned (40 shuffled tables max 40.5%). Independent sample R14-R18: 88.1%, controls max 51.5%.
cc. 78r-79r and 174r-175v transcribed in two passes, not blind to the table; 314 of 7,870 signs differ, 36 lines re-read on crops.

Independent agent, blind to the transcription, not to the table: 22 lines, 917 signs, raw disagreement 8.4%, our transcription wrong on 2.1-2.6% after settling on crops. A lower bound. A separate decoder reproduces all 174 lines.
Third pass: 60 logged sign changes, from the check, a shape-only sweep of g against z, n/u after p, and crops at each repair. No new error sample after these.
Readings rewritten with 18 marked repairs; a letter-by-letter check reports no unmarked departure from the signs. c. 175r kept as decoded, not read.
Web searches found no edition. Murphy, Furlotti, Solmi and the Mantua copialettere were not opened.
Catalogue 1554: ten cipher pages of cc. 113-120 fetched by IIIF at full resolution. No decipherment, docket, address or clear word on the leaves.
Catalogue 1554: two passes, table known, differing on 429 of 8,390 signs (5.1%); twelve edits settled on crops, the rest not re-read.
Catalogue 1554: frozen table against 500 shuffled tables on each of ten pages. Every page beats all 500 on the bigram score. The word-hit count ties the shuffled maximum on c. 116r.
Catalogue 1554, first design: ciphertext-only attack that let several signs share one letter. It beat the true table and agreed with it on almost nothing; dropped as overfit.
Catalogue 1554, second design: strict one-to-one attack with no table as input. 20 of 20 signs agree on all letters together; short letters c. 114r and c. 116r fall short (18 and 13 of 20).

Catalogue 1554: separate agent read five lines of c. 119r, the page with the worst pass agreement, blind to the transcription, not to the table or the summary: 194 signs, raw disagreement 23.7%; after settling on crops the transcription was wrong on 20.6%, the blind reading on 5.7%. The five lines were corrected; the other 193 lines were not checked.
Catalogue 1554: working readings have 1 sentence block without a hole in 51, so all seven letters stay decoded, not read. The working readings are not in this folder.
Catalogue 1554: three web searches found no edition or decipherment; no book was opened.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The table was built by aligning c. 103r with the contemporary decipherment on c. 104r in the same sub-file, frozen, tested on c. 109r against c. 107, then applied to the two letters that have no decipherment. Catalogue 1554 applies the same table unchanged; it contributed nothing to the key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: scripts/count_words.py: 1,021 of about 2,141 words stand in sentences with no [...], on the leaves read in part (385 of 786 on cc. 78r-79r, 636 of 1,023 on cc. 174r, 174v, 175v). c. 175r counts as not read. Those sentences may still hold proposals. In fully clean sentences: 184 and 199 words, and 61 on c. 175r. Word totals are estimates: letters divided by 4.35. The seven letters of catalogue 1554 are decoded, not read and are outside this figure.

texts.label: Ercole Gonzaga to Ferrante Gonzaga, Mantua, 4 May 1544, cc. 78r-79r
texts.summary: Three weeks after Ceresole. Ercole explains his orders for Casale and Monferrato, weighs losing Monferrato against risking Mantua, fears seeming a friend of fortune, and protests his duty as a vassal. He then reports on the count of Mirandola, Piero Strozzi and talk of Tuscany.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. The letter's line of argument can be followed in Italian and English: the orders for Casale, the fear of losing Monferrato against risking Mantua, the fear of seeming a friend of fortune, his duty as a vassal, and the Mirandola news about the cardinal of Ferrara, Strozzi and Tuscany. About ten of the 24 blocks have holes, and several are broken where they start or in the middle (A05-A06, A16-A19, B22-B24, C03-C06, C10). Key words such as his Majesty and the emperor are proposals from context, and the codes [L^30] and [L^22], which carry much of the meaning, are not identified. The spelling is raw and the English is strained in places (A21-A24).

texts.label: Ercole Gonzaga to Ferrante Gonzaga, undated, cc. 174r, 174v, 175v
texts.summary: Ercole says his intelligence on the Pope is ill received by the Emperor's ministers and asks Ferrante whether to go on. He relays the Pope's complaint over the diet and Busseto and the Emperor's answer. c. 175v turns to the sequestration of revenues of cardinals who serve France, and Salviati. The reading file also prints c. 175r, which is not claimed as read.

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. On c. 174r and most of c. 174v the Italian reads as connected sentences with only scattered holes: his intelligence on the Pope gets a poor welcome, the Pope complains over the diet and Busseto, the Emperor answers, and Ercole asks whether he should go on. On c. 175v the opening blocks G02-G07 do not form sentences, and the ends of E10-E13 and E24-F02 are rough. After G07 the text is coherent again (Salviati, the sequestration, the count of Mirandola). Weak points: emperor and his Majesty are proposed readings of codes, '[?copie] parole' is translated loosely as 'many good words', and the codes [43] and [L^6] stay unidentified.

texts.label: Same letter, c. 175r
texts.summary: Only F02-F06 and F16-F17 run as sentences. The rest seems to concern plans of the Pope around Milan and Tuscany. Its lines stand in reading_0174_0175.md under a heading that says so.
